title: Opaque-cache reconciliation orchestrator for zero-rt rollback during private runtime switchover
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: Goal: implement an orchestrator that performs runtime/data-plane rollouts in VPC/private deployments with zero observable RT (response-time) regression and deterministic rollback. Key idea: treat node-local KV/prefix caches as opaque state, reconcile them with a checkpointed snapshot and run traffic shadowing + incremental attach/detach so that a failed upgrade can be reverted without client-visible latency or session corruption.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Upgrade flow can perform a tenant slice switchover with no 99th-percentile latency regression >10% for requests that hit primed caches
2) Orchestrator supports per-tenant 'opaque-cache-reconcile' hook that ensures runtime receives KV snapshot and validates priming before accepting production traffic
3) Automated rollback completes within configured SLA (default 90s) and leaves no dangling sessions or inconsistent KV materialization
4) Terraform module exposes inputs for preflight check toggles, health gating thresholds, and a 'shadow_ratio' for mirrored traffic
5) End-to-end tests in CI simulate failed priming and validate automated rollback triggers and post-rollback health restoration
implementation_notes: We will implement a new controller in the private operator (go) with the following responsibilities: compute tenant slice order, apply 'snapshot-and-seal' RPC to source slice, create ephemeral priming job on target slice that pulls checkpoint, run shadowed traffic at configurable rate, and promote on health quorum
KV checkpointing: extend existing snapshot API to include per-slot opaque checksums and priming manifest (list of hot prefixes + byte-range hints).

Terraform/IaC: add module 'redwood_private_rollout' that wires operator feature flags, lifecycle hooks for snapshot export (S3/GCS or internal blobstore), and a 'drain_window_seconds' default used by rolling policy.

Safety: health quorum requires synthetic probes, priming progress metrics (keys per second), and connection stability (socket churn). Default thresholds are conservative — will be tuned by QA runbook.
Observability: emit rollout_id, slice_id, priming_progress_pct, kv_checksum_match (boolean), and rollback_reason to Console and to rollout-specific logs for postmortem.
Trade-off: a higher shadow_ratio reduces risk of unseen regressions but increases cost. We default to 10% for canaries, 50% for tenant-local full cutovers when priming is fast.

Decision log: we chose opaque reconciliation vs direct streaming of KV entries to avoid high memory pressure on target nodes and to keep network burst predictable. This allows pre-warming with compact manifests rather than full dump at once.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Preflight: Terraform plan applies module in dry-run, operator validates blobstore access, and system creates rollout_id with dry=true; CI runs preflight suite (integration + synthetic probes).
Phase 1 - Snapshot and Seal: source slice receives 'snapshot-and-seal' RPC; snapshot manifest uploaded to configured blobstore. Snapshot includes checksum and manifest of hot prefixes.
Phase 2 - Target Priming: operator schedules priming job on target slice, pulls snapshot and performs black-box priming using manifest hints; priming exposes metrics via rollout_id.

Phase 3 - Shadow Traffic: proxy config updated to mirror configured shadow_ratio of production traffic to target slice while replies are discarded from response path. Continuous priming and probe validations run for min(30s, priming_estimate).

Phase 4 - Promotion: when health quorum satisfied (synthetic probes green, priming_progress >= 95%, checksum match), traffic gradually shifts to target using split routing (10% increments, 30s windows) with active KV reconciliation hooks running in background.
Phase 5 - Post-promote stabilization: monitor for errors for 10m; if any critical health metric crosses threshold, automated rollback triggers.

Phase 6 - Rollback (if needed): orchestrator initiates reverse-attach and drains new nodes using 'graceful session cutover' so active requests continue on source; then target nodes are demoted and priming artifacts flagged for garbage collection.
health_checks: Priming progress: keys/sec and effective coverage of hot prefix manifest (target must reach >=95% of expected hot key accesses)
KV checksum validation: boolean match between source manifest checksum and target delta checksum
Synthetic probe suite: latency P95/P99, error rate, and deterministic correctness checks for a fixed prompt set
Connection stability: socket churn rate and average connection lifetime must not regress beyond configured deltas
Memory and swap pressure: node-level memory high-water marks must remain below 85% during priming
Traffic mirror validation: probe responses from target must match source within allowed fuzzy thresholds for correctness metrics
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback trigger conditions: checksum mismatch, priming stalls > configured timeout, synthetic probe failures above threshold, or operator cancel

Rollback steps: 1) Quiesce new target traffic attach (stop promotion), 2) Re-attach traffic to original slice using immediate routing rule, 3) Drain target slice gracefully waiting for in-flight requests < configured threshold, 4) Mark rollout as aborted and capture detailed snapshot for postmortem, 5) Run background reconciliation to repair any partial priming artifacts
Time budget: complete rollback decision and network-level routing flip within 90s; full drain and cleanup aim for <10 minutes depending on active sessions

Emergency escape hatch: if automated rollback cannot reach quorum (e.g., control-plane partition), operator can perform manual cutover using the 'emergency-attach' terraform variable to force immediate routing revert
Post-rollback verification: run a focused synthetic probe run and KV checksum compare to confirm state parity before marking rollout as failed/done
testing_plan: Unit tests for operator controller loops and snapshot manifest generation (go test)
Integration harness in staging: end-to-end rollout with varying shadow_ratio values and induced priming latency; assert metrics and SLOs
Chaos tests: introduce network partition between operator and blobstore during priming; validate retry/backoff and eventual rollback
Performance tests: run priming at scale with realistic hot-prefix distributions to ensure memory and network bounds are respected
CI gating: require green for rollout feature branch PR before terraform module is merged to main; include nightly fuzz-run for rollback conditions
dependencies: ENG-412356 (vpc incremental runtime migration synthetic health)
Blobstore team: export API and client libs for snapshot publish/consume
risks: Priming large KV footprints may temporarily spike egress costs and network saturation in customer VPCs
Incorrect checksum logic could cause false positives that trigger rollbacks unnecessarily
Operator bugs could leave partial primed targets that require manual GC, increasing toil
Shadow traffic increases request surface area and could reveal non-deterministic models or race conditions not seen in single-slice operation
